chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Makfuf narrated to me; he said: Some of our companions narrated to me from some of the phlebotomists of al-ʿAskar who were Christians.

That Abu Muhammad عليه السلام sent for me one day at the time of Salat al-Zuhr and said to me, "Perform phlebotomy on this vein." He then showed me a vein that I did not recognize among the veins that are usually opened. So I said to myself, "I have never seen a matter stranger than this: he is ordering me to perform phlebotomy at the time of Zuhr, though it is not a time for phlebotomy, and secondly it is a vein I do not know."

Then he said to me, "Wait and remain in the house." When evening came, he called me and said, "Release the blood." So I released it. Then he said to me, "Stop," so I stopped. Then he said to me, "Remain in the house." When it was midnight, he sent for me and said to me, "Release the blood." He said: I was even more astonished than at my first astonishment, and I disliked to ask him. He said: So I released it, and white blood came out as though it were salt. He then said to me, "Restrain it," so I restrained it. Then he said, "Remain in the house."

When morning came, he ordered his steward to give me three dinars. I took them and went out until I came to Ibn Bakhtishuʿ the Christian, and I recounted the story to him. He said to me, "By Allah, I do not understand what you are saying, nor do I recognize it in any branch of medicine, nor have I read it in any book. And I do not know in our time anyone more knowledgeable about the books of the Christians than so-and-so the Persian, so go to him." He said: So I hired a boat to al-Basrah, went to al-Ahwaz, then proceeded to فارس to my companion and informed him of the report. He said, "Give me some days." So I gave him time. Then I came to him asking for the answer. He said to me, "This that you are relating from this man was done once by al-Masih in his time."

key_terms.افْصِدْ: perform phlebotomy; open a vein to let blood flow
key_terms.الْعِرْقَ: the vein indicated for the procedure
key_terms.الْمَسِيحُ: the Messiah, cited as having performed such an act once in his time
key_terms.دَمٌ أَبْيَضُ: white blood, described as an extraordinary occurrence
key_terms.سَرِّحِ الدَّمَ: release the blood; allow the blood to flow
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الظُّهْرِ: the noon salat, the time at which the Imam عليه السلام summoned the phlebotomist
key_terms.قَهْرَمَانَهُ: his steward or household agent entrusted with payment

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Kafi relate about the extraordinary sign shown by Imam al-Hasan al-ʿAskari عليه السلام to a Christian phlebotomist?
ai.summary: This narration recounts an extraordinary medical act witnessed from Abu Muhammad عليه السلام by a Christian phlebotomist, who found it contrary to known medical practice and beyond his understanding. After consulting learned Christian physicians, the event was described as something previously done only by al-Masih, highlighting the exceptional status and knowledge of the Imam عليه السلام.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Al Husayn who said, ‘Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Al Makfouf who said, ‘Some of our companions narrated to me from some cuppers of Al-Askar (who were) from the Christians

and that Abu Muhammadasws (11th Imamasws) sent for me one day during the time of Al-Zahor Salat and he said to me, ‘Get cupping done of this vein’, and heasws pointed out a vein which I did not understand from the veins which do get cupped. So I said, within myself, ‘I have not seen a matter stranger than this. Heasws is ordering me that I should get cupping done during this time of Al-Zohr and it isn’t a time for cupping, and secondly it is a vein which I do not recognise’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Await and stay in the house’. So when it was evening, he<sup>asws</sup> called me over and said to me: ‘Release the blood’. So I (cut the vein and) released it. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Withhold!’ So I withheld. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Stay in the house. So when it was half the night, he<sup>asws</sup> sent for me and said to me: ‘Release the blood’. So I was astounded even more than my first astonishment, and I disliked to ask him<sup>asws</sup>. So I released (the blood) and the blood came out white as if it was salt. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Withhold!’ So I withheld. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Stay in the house’.

So when we were in the morning, he<sup>asws</sup> ordered his<sup>asws</sup> clerk to give me three Dinars. So I took these and went out until I came to Ibn Bakhtayshou the Christian, and I related to him the story. So he said to me, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I don’t understand what you are saying nor do I recognise it regarding anything from the medicine (treatments), nor have I read it in a book, nor do I know in our times anyone more knowledgeable with the books of the Christians than so and so, the Persian. Therefore, go out to him’.  He (the narrator) said, ‘So I hired a boat to Al-Basra, and I went over to Ahvaz, then I came to Persia to my companion and I informed him of the news. He said, ‘Respite me for some days’. So I waited for him, then went over to him requesting. So he said to me, ‘This which you are relating from this man, the Messiah<sup>as</sup> had done it once during his<sup>as</sup> time’.
en.sarwar: 23. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim ibn Musa ibn Ja‘far ibn Muhammad (a.s.) from Ali ibn ‘Abd al-Ghaffar who has said the following.

“When abu Muhammad (a.s.) was imprisoned, the ‘Abbassids, Salih ibn Wasif, Salih ibn Ali and others who were not Shi‘as all came to Salih ibn Wasif asking him to exert more pressure on abu Muhammad (a.s.).

Salih told them, “What should I do? I managed to find two people who were of the harshest manners and appointed them to guard him they both turned into most assiduous worshippers in prayers and fasting. When I asked them about their behaviors they replied, “What would you say about a man who fasts every day, worships the whole night and does not speak or busy himself with anything? When we look at him a feeling of trembling and shivering over takes us and we lose control over our own selves.”
When they heard this they returned in despair.”
